title: A prospective, randomized clinical trial in split mouth design analyzing the influence of an autologous fibrin matrix (PRF) on wound healing and bone regeneration after osteotomy of displaced and retained third molars
summary:
In some cases wisdom teeth can’t come in at the right place, or they can’t come in at all, because of retainment or other unknown reasons, making the extraction of the tooth necessary. This results in a wound in need to be taken care of. The bone in which the tooth was embedded needs be regenerated as well. The primary aim is therefore to treat such a wound, the so-called extraction socket, in a way that a fast, efficient, and if possible painless wound healing, and bone regeneration can be achieved. The so-called platelet rich fibrin (PRF), enriched in blood components as thrombocytes, leucocytes and plasma proteins, can be used for improving wound healing and bone regeneration.
Out of PRF, a blood concentrate obtained from centrifugation of patients own blood, a solid membrane, containing cell rich fractions of the blood, can be prepared, which is then used as filling material for the extraction socket. 
In this study we aim to compare the conventional treatment of extraction sockets primary closed by suture to the additional treatment of the defect with the blood concentrate PRF, obtained from patients own blood.
conditions: Loss of teeth due to accident, extraction or local periodontal disease

interventions.name: Treatment Group 1 - PRF high, Socket Preservation after tooth extraction with PRF prepared at high g-force
Treatment Group 2 - PRF medium, Socket Preservation after tooth extraction with PRF prepared at medium g-force
Treatment Group 3 - PRF low, Socket Preservation after tooth extraction with PRF prepared according to LSCC (low speed centrifugation concept)
